- To this point, we've worked with individual mass spectra (as a representative measurement) - we looked at loading the measurement - plotting it - processing it (e.g., removing peaks) - interpreting it (e.g., identifying the base peak, identifying significant peaks)

- In addition to looking at individual measurements, we often want to compare measurements ## Comparing two mass spectra - Load and plot two mass spectra ::: {.fragment} ```{r} SpecA = read.table("U1.txt") mzA = SpecA[,1] intA = SpecA[,2]/max(SpecA[,2]) SpecB = read.table("U2.txt") mzB = SpecB[,1] intB = SpecB[,2]/max(SpecB[,2]) ``` ```{r} #| eval: false plot(mzA, intA, type="h", xlab="mass-to-charge ratio", ylab="relative intensity") plot(mzB, intB, type="h", xlab="mass-to-charge ratio", ylab="relative intensity") ``` ::: ## Comparing two mass spectra - In MS, it is common to create *head-to-tail* plots to compare and contrast mass spectra ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: false minx = min(mzA,mzB) maxx = max(mzA,mzB) plot(mzA, intA, type="h", xlab="mass-to-charge ratio", ylab="relative intensity", xlim=c(minx,maxx), ylim=c(-1,1), col="purple") matplot(mzB, -intB, type="h", col="blue", add=TRUE) ``` ::: ## Comparing two mass spectra - When we compare and contrast data, we are really looking for similarities and differences - number of common peaks? - number of common major peaks? - fraction of common major peaks compared to all peaks? - fraction of total relative intensity accounted for by common peaks?

- **IMPORTANT:** We need to explicitly define metrics of similarity (or differences) to support rigorous comparison and transparent communications ## On vectors - Vectors are mathematical objects that can be thought of as *points* in higher dimensional space - E.g., used in chemistry and physics to describe objects with multiple properties (e.g., magnitude and direction)

- From geometry, we have some standard methods for comparing vectors

- Consider the 2D vectors (1,5) and (7,3) ## Comparing vectors ![](../figures/simAnddist_2d_vectors.png) ## Comparing vectors - *Distance* - How far are the vectors in n-dimensional space - **Euclidean Distance: ** $d(x,y) = \sqrt{\sum_i^n(x_i-y_i)^2}$

- *Similarity* - A function of the angle between the vectors in n-dimensional space - **Cosine Similarity: ** $s(x,y) = \frac{\sum_i^n x_iy_i}{\sqrt{\sum_i^n x_i^2}\sqrt{\sum_i^n y_i^2}}$ ## Comparing vectors ```{r} #| eval: false A = c(1,5) B = c(7,3) ED = sqrt(sum((A-B)^2)) CS = sum(A*B)/(sqrt(sum(A*A))*sqrt(sum(B*B))) cat(paste0("The euclidean distance between vectors A and B is ",round(ED,3),"\n")) cat(paste0("The cosine similarity between vectors A and B is ",round(CS,3),"\n")) ``` ```{r} #| eval: false A = c(1,5,5,7,6,8) B = c(7,3,2,8,9,1) ED = sqrt(sum((A-B)^2)) CS = sum(A*B)/(sqrt(sum(A*A))*sqrt(sum(B*B))) cat(paste0("The euclidean distance between vectors A and B is ",round(ED,3),"\n")) cat(paste0("The cosine similarity between vectors A and B is ",round(CS,3),"\n")) ``` ```{r} #| eval: false A = c(1,5,0,0) B = c(7,3,0,0) ED = sqrt(sum((A-B)^2)) CS = sum(A*B)/(sqrt(sum(A*A))*sqrt(sum(B*B))) cat(paste0("The euclidean distance between vectors A and B is ",round(ED,3),"\n")) cat(paste0("The cosine similarity between vectors A and B is ",round(CS,3),"\n")) ``` ## From mass spectra to vectors - If we can represent our mass spectral measurements as **comparable** vectors, we can use the idea of distances and similarities as an objective way to compare mass spectra

- a standard approach with low-resolution (integer resolution) mass spectra is to create vectors that are the length of the highest *m/z* value and populate the vector such that the value at each index of the vector is the intensity from the corresponding *m/z* in the spectrum ## From mass spectra to vectors ```{r} #| eval: true SpecA = read.table("U1.txt") mzA = SpecA[,1] intA = SpecA[,2]/max(SpecA[,2]) A = numeric(max(mzA)) # create a numeric vector the length of the highest mass to charge ratio in A filled with zeros A[129:136] for(i in 1:length(mzA)){ A[mzA[i]] = intA[i] } A[129:136] ``` ## From mass spectra to vectors - **IMPORTANT:** When comparing two vectors, they must be of the same dimension - If two mass spectra have different highest mass-to-charge ratios; we make sure the vectors created by these mass spectra take the length of the higher of the two mass-to-charge ratios ## From mass spectra to vectors ```{r} #| eval: true SpecA = read.table("U1.txt") mzA = SpecA[,1] intA = SpecA[,2]/max(SpecA[,2]) SpecB = read.table("U2.txt") mzB = SpecB[,1] intB = SpecB[,2]/max(SpecB[,2]) maxMz = max(c(mzA,mzB)) A = numeric(maxMz) B = numeric(maxMz) for(i in 1:length(mzA)){ A[mzA[i]] = intA[i] } for(i in 1:length(mzB)){ B[mzB[i]] = intB[i] } ED = sqrt(sum((A-B)^2)) CS = sum(A*B)/(sqrt(sum(A*A))*sqrt(sum(B*B))) cat(paste0("The euclidean distance between vectors A and B is ",round(ED,3),"\n")) cat(paste0("The cosine similarity between vectors A and B is ",round(CS,3),"\n")) ``` ## From mass spectra to vectors - We can be selective (and more efficient) when constructing a vector embedding of a mass spectrum - [Domain-segmented similarity score](https://chemrxiv.org/doi/abs/10.26434/chemrxiv.15007342/v2){target="_blank"}: This is a new article I wrote where we are trying to use contextual knowledge when comparing high resolution mass spectra

- We can also experiment with other measures of similarity and distances - [Pattern similarity measures](https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=929428){target="_blank"}: This is an old article I wrote where we compare several standard measures of similarity used in pattern recognition to more "customized" measures found in the mass spectrometry literature ## Coming up - Seminars are running in-person on Thursday November 5th
- 5-7 PM (SC 204) and 8-10 PM (SC W1)

- **Next week:** Projections and dimensionality reduction - Looking at a set of more than 2 measurements
